sentences.text: The holotype specimen includes parts of the skull, jaw, vertebrae, limbs, and armor plates, revealing an animal covered in body armor made of osteoderms. Like Scelidosaurus, it had protective armor consisting of a very hard skin riveted with strong, round scales.
Its small head ended in a horny beak with leaf-shaped teeth that allowed it to strip buds and low plants. The armor included three conical shields and a tall, spiny element.

Emausaurus forelimbs were adapted for weight support rather than grasping, with conical, slightly curved claws. Evidence suggests Emausaurus was a quadrupedal, low-roaming herbivore adapted for supporting its weight.
When walking, it kept its tail held upright.
The juvenile holotype of Emausaurus was estimated to be 2 to 2.5 meters long and weigh between 50 and 90 kilograms, while adults reached lengths of 3 to 4 meters and weights up to 240 kilograms.
An adult Emausaurus was a small armored dinosaur measuring 4 meters long, 0.70 meters high, and weighing 30 kilograms.
Emausaurus possessed a sinuous jaw profile, a feature more advanced than that of the basal genus Scutellosaurus.
Fossils of Emausaurus were found in the Lehmhagen Member in northern Germany, specifically in Bituminous Shale in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern.

The holotype was found in a Lower Toarcian shale layer at the Emausaurus type site, where geologist Werner Ernst found the holotype fossil SGWG 85 in the summer of 1963 near a lake in Grimmen within Toarcian strata.

The species Emausaurus ernsti was named and described by Hartmut Haubold in 1990, though later sources note the formal description occurred in 1991. The specific name is also in honor of the Ernst Moritz Arndt University.
Emausaurus was likely a low-browsing herbivore that ate cycads and Bennettitales.
Although few osteoderms have been found, they indicate Emausaurus was covered in armor, though the extent of coverage is unknown.

Cladistic analyses place Emausaurus as a basal member of the Thyreophora, between Scutellosaurus and Scelidosaurus. Cladistic analyses showed that Emausaurus was a basal member of Thyreophora, more derived than Scutellosaurus but less derived than Scelidosaurus.
Its parent group is Scelidosauridae, and it belongs to the family Scelidosauridae. It is classified in the class Ornithischia.

Emausaurus is the only known armored dinosaur from the Toarcian stage of the Early Jurassic. Emausaurus lived approximately 185 million years ago during the Early Jurassic Toarcian in what is now Europe.
It lived during the Toarcian stage, between 184.2 and 182.9 million years ago.
The fossil site contains invertebrates including insects, bivalves, sea snails, and ammonites. Fish fossils from the site include the genera Saurorhynchus, Grimmenichthys, and Grimmenodon.

The phylogenetic position of Emausaurus is controversial because the known specimen is immature. Researchers have debated whether Emausaurus is more derived than Scelidosaurus or a sister taxon to Stegosauria. Later studies criticize assumptions of bipedality or quadrupedality in Emausaurus due to its incomplete nature and close relationship with Scutellosaurus.
